action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's budget posture is to scale up acquisition: the long-run uptrend is intact, and this kind of phase has historically been when spending to win new and returning users paid back best, especially among active traders. Apply it in measured steps for now: price bounced this week but is still about 2% under its 50-day average after 15 days below it, the mood is a neutral 50 out of 100, and the US election result makes clear US crypto rules slower to arrive. So add spend gradually, keep part of the increase ready to pause, lead with trust and everyday-use stories, and speed up once price closes back above about $82,111. This is a budget-timing guide for the business, not trading advice.

analysis: Bottom line: the long-run uptrend still holds and Bitcoin bounced this week, but the short term is soft to neutral until price gets back above its 50-day average. Bitcoin rose about 4% in the last day to around $80,768, yet it has now closed under that average for 15 days and sits about 2% below it and about 4% under its 30-day high; the mood is exactly middling, with Fear & Greed at 50. A normal week swings about $3,352, so a close above $82,111 (the 50-day average) would turn it clearly up, a close below $79,000 (bottom of a typical week's swing) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy; for the bigger picture, $73,222 (the 200-day average) is the floor. Binance says it has replaced about 98% of the stolen coins and Mercado Bitcoin plans to reopen from 9 November, so safety worries are easing, and winning back that average is what would make the week look firm.

The next month is mixed. The 90-day numbers still point up, with price about 24% higher and about 88% of those days closing above the long-term average, but the last 30 days are down about 6%. Price must win back $82,111 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there room to climb further; while it stays under that average, the month keeps fading. News is taking a little off here: Democrats won both houses of the US Congress, and the pending US crypto rules bill now expires on 3 January 2027 unless it finds 60 Senate votes (PANews citing The Block); the next Fed meeting is 8 December, so keep bigger campaign pushes for that reclaim.

The 3-6 month picture leans up at a moderate strength. Price is about 10% above its 200-day average and that average is still rising, about 4% over 90 days, while Bitcoin remains about 35% below its all-time high. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $73,222 (the 200-day average); if that goes, $67,307 (the 200-week average) is the next floor, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. News adds a little to this picture, led by Stripe letting US businesses pay people in digital dollars straight to crypto wallets in over 160 markets, and a close below the 200-day average is what would weaken it and be the moment to shift budget toward keeping existing users.

items.why: Democrats won control of both houses of the US Congress, and Bloomberg (via PANews) reports this hit politically linked crypto assets: the TRUMP meme coin fell sharply and Trump Media shares hit a record low. Reports also say the pending US crypto rules bill expires on 3 January 2027 unless it wins 60 Senate votes.
items.marketing_angle: A plain explainer on what the new US Congress means for crypto rules is timely; avoid political framing.

items.why: Stripe now lets eligible US businesses pay people in USDC straight to their crypto wallets in over 160 markets (PANews citing The Defiant), and Circle says USDC makes up 79% of stablecoin transaction volume. Large new batches of USDC and USDT were also moved onto Solana and to Binance this week.
items.marketing_angle: Good material for an everyday-use story on how digital dollars move across borders, aimed at newer users.

items.theme: Shares in token form keep moving ahead
items.why: A US court refused to pause the futures regulator's approval of single-stock contracts on crypto-style venues, Canton Network completed the first tokenized US stock trades under the SEC's new exemption, and Aave now accepts a tokenized SpaceX share as collateral. The sources tie these to rule changes, not to a token price move.

items.why: The largest exchange says it has replaced almost all stolen coins and widened its public reserve check, and Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin says it will start reopening from 9 November, which eases the immediate safety worry.

items.headline: Analysis: Democrats Take Control of US Congress, Crypto Industry Faces New Regulatory Headwinds
items.why: With Democrats winning both chambers, the pending US crypto market rules bill (Clarity Act) expires on 3 January 2027 unless it gets 60 Senate votes, so the path to clear US rules is now slower and less certain.

items.headline: US Court Denies Request for Temporary Restraining Order to Pause Single-Stock Perpetual Contracts
items.why: A court refused to pause the US futures regulator's approval of a crypto-born contract type on regulated venues, so that product can go ahead while the lawsuit continues.

items.headline: France's National Assembly passes amendment that would require declaring self-custodied crypto assets above €100,000
items.why: A large European market moves toward making people report big crypto holdings kept in their own wallets to the tax office; it is part of a budget bill not yet final.

items.headline: Stripe Enables US Businesses to Send Stablecoins to Crypto Wallets in Over 160 Markets
items.why: One of the biggest payment companies now lets businesses pay people in digital dollars straight to their crypto wallets across 160+ markets, a real-world use that widens everyday crypto payments.

items.headline: Coinbase Prime Launches Global Options and Perpetual Futures Trading for US Institutions
items.why: Large US institutions get a regulated way to use more crypto products through a major exchange, another step in big-money access.

summary.short: Exchanges recovering from last week's thefts is a small plus for the week.
summary.medium: Democrats winning the US Congress slows the path to clear US crypto rules, only partly offset by a court letting a new product type go ahead, so news is a small minus for the month.
summary.long: Stripe's digital-dollar payouts and Coinbase opening more products to US institutions add a little to the long-run picture.
